text:
Nora: Quick live thread for Qs we didn't get to in today's all-hands about positioning and the roadmap.

Ben: Topline ask from sales: what's the short elevator pitch that differentiates us from big cloud endpoints and from teams that self-host runtimes?

Sofia: Suggestion: 'Inference you can count on: predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and an easy path from hosted to dedicated/private.'

Diego: Engineering nuance: call out that "predictable" = optional reserved capacity + runtime controls (batching, caching) rather than a hard guarantee for every workload.

Nora: Agreed. We'll use that language and include a short line on trade-offs in collateral.

Ben: Competitor framing idea: compare across three axes: cost transparency, operational burden, and SLA options. Keep it non-branded.

Sofia: Also include a short note on graceful degradation: defaults are conservative, fallbacks require opt-in and will notify users. Example for docs: `fallback_policy: opt_in` (code snippet).

Diego: Roadmap ask: can we publish rough prioritization? My suggested order: 1) runtime perf & kernel tuning, 2) observability + rollouts, 3) migration tooling.

Nora: Leadership okayed sharing those priorities externally as high-level intents. We'll avoid specific % targets in public docs but engineering can provide internal benchmarks.

ops-bot: Meeting notes uploaded: /files/all-hands/1733339999-followups.pdf :page_with_curl:

Nora: I'll post a draft 1-pager with the hero line "Inference you can count on" and a three-bullet competitor comparison by EOD Tuesday. Please DM me edits. :sparkles:
